To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we derived an analytic expression for shear viscosity of an ultrarelativistic gas with isotropic elastic 2→2 and inelastic scattering processes, and we showed that the values of shear viscosity obtained from kinetic transport simulations agree with our analytic formula.

we derived the shear viscosity of a gas of ultra-relativistic particles undergoing elastic 2 →2 and inelastic (e.g. annihilation) processes with isotropic cross sections, and that the obtained formula agrees with the shear viscosity extracted from kinetic calculations.

we derive a formula for the shear viscosity coefficient of an ultrarelatedivistic Boltz- mann gas with both elastic and inelastic scattering processes, and that the obtained formula is in excellent agreement with kinetic transport calculations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the derivation of an analytic expression for a shear viscosity coefficient for a gas with both elastic and inelastic scattering processes in the framework of the Boltzmann equation.
the shear viscosity coefficient of a relativistic gas in presence both elastic and inelastic collisions.
a Boltzmann gas in presence of isotropic inelastic 2 → 3 scattering processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the absence of a rigorous derivation of the transport coefficients, one should always use the kinetic theory approach to compute them.

the analytic expression for the viscosity coefficient derived here, based on the entropy and the Grad approximation for the off equilibrium distribution function, provides a very good description of the shear viscosity of a relativistic gas, in presence of both 2 → 1 and 2 → 3 processes, with isotropic differential scattering cross sections.
the Green–Kubos formula is a very good approximation for the shear viscosity coefficient, and that the entropy principle is a good approximation for the transport coefficients of a Boltzmann gas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the shear viscosity of a relativistic gas with isotropic scattering can be calculated from the total cross sections alone, i.e. it is independent of the details of the collision dynamics.
the analytic formula derived here is a generalization of the Chapman–Enskog result to the inelastic case and that the kinetic transport calculations confirm the validity of this formula.
the entropy principle provides a simple, reliable, and robust method to derive analytic expressions for the transport coefficients of an ultrarelatedivistic gas in presence inelastic processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the shear viscosity coefficient is not a function of the elastic cross section σ 22 alone.
, for a Boltzmann gas, inelastic processes do not contribute to the shear viscosity.
the inelastic scattering processes can be included in the calculation of shear viscosity without introducing additional phenomenological parameters.
